challenge.better_approach: Considered catching RuntimeError in Ticket.queueme and matching its text. That puts the fix in the wrong component, and every other bus_client caller would keep the wrong kind. The client owns its error mapping, and it already maps LookupError.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That no caller relies on a bus-process timeout being a RuntimeError. git grep shows the RuntimeError catchers in codemother's stage machines read berths, not the bus, and no code matches 'bus process: TimeoutError'.
challenge.prior_art: 0bcb816d6e9c built the wait-on-the-berth path after a reply timeout. Its proof patches participant.request to raise TimeoutError directly, so it never went through RemoteBus and never saw the wrapping. remote.py already maps LookupError back.
challenge.real_collision: none: TimeoutError is a subclass of OSError, not RuntimeError, so a caller that caught only RuntimeError around a bus call would now see the exception escape. None was found by grep.

answers.falsifier: A bus-process 'TimeoutError: <words>' raises TimeoutError with the same words, through RemoteBus and through reach(), far and local. Every other error keeps its kind (RuntimeError or LookupError).
answers.from_idea: none, because this was measured, not imagined: q79.log in /tmp/claude-1000/-home-akien-dev-src-cairn/546bccde-fde2-48b2-9435-eaf9605f128f/scratchpad/q79.log, line 24, 'RuntimeError: bus process: TimeoutError: no reply to envelope 09d15224…'
answers.how: In cairn/tools/bus_client/remote.py RemoteBus._call, an error starting 'TimeoutError: ' is raised as TimeoutError with the prefix removed, the way 'LookupError: ' is already mapped. A red-first proof replaces remote.exchange and checks the kind through RemoteBus and through reach(), far and local.
answers.traces_to: Law 7: errors stay what they are in a diagnostic surface. Here a timeout was renamed into a RuntimeError, which hid it from the one caller built to wait it out (ticket 0bcb816d6e9c).
answers.what: A timeout inside the bus process reaches the bus_client's caller as a TimeoutError, so a ticket asking a slow chart or verdict gate waits on its own berth instead of dying at the reply timeout.

bullets.text: 149b's PROVED was refused because sail died at 890 s while codemother's verdict was still running. The ticket's 3600 s berth wait never ran, because bus_client renamed the TimeoutError into a RuntimeError.
